questions.q: Why does this lesson say data architecture is broader than just object and field design?
options: Because object and field design has nothing to do with data architecture
Because Salesforce does not allow custom objects in data architecture discussions
Because it also covers data volume's effect on performance, master data ownership, and ongoing data quality and governance
Because field design is handled exclusively by developers, never architects
questions.explain: Object and field design is a real part of data architecture, but the domain also covers how volume affects performance over time, which system owns the truth for shared data, and how data quality is maintained as the business operates.

questions.q: What does this lesson identify as the actual architectural mistake regarding data volume, rather than failing to predict an exact future number?
options: Failing to ask the volume question at all during design, only discovering the answer once the org is already struggling under real production load
Choosing the wrong field type for a currency field
Using too many custom objects in a data model
Allowing more than one profile to access the same object
questions.explain: Nobody can predict an exact future volume precisely, but an architect should still ask roughly how much data a design will hold and whether its behavior at that scale matters — skipping that question entirely, not an imprecise estimate, is the real mistake.

questions.q: What is master data management, as this lesson defines it?
options: A Salesforce feature for backing up all data automatically
A synonym for data volume planning
The process of deleting duplicate records after they're created
Deciding which system is the authoritative source of truth for a given piece of shared data, and how changes propagate from it
questions.explain: When the same information exists in more than one system, master data management is the deliberate decision about which system owns the truth for it and how updates flow from that source to everywhere else that holds a copy.

questions.q: What happens without a deliberate master data decision, per this lesson's pricing example?
options: Nothing; Salesforce automatically resolves conflicting data between systems
Two systems can quietly disagree about the same piece of information, with no way to tell which one is actually correct
The ERP system is always automatically treated as correct by default
Data volume becomes irrelevant once master data is defined
questions.explain: Without deciding which system is authoritative, two systems holding the same data (like a product's price) can drift out of sync with no principled way to know which value is actually correct — a classic, expensive data-integrity failure.

questions.q: How does this lesson connect data architecture to data quality and governance?
options: It says data quality is entirely unrelated to data architecture
It claims governance only applies after a system is decommissioned

A technically well-designed data model can still fail in practice without enforced data quality (validation, duplicate management, deliberately required fields), and structural decisions affect how sensitive data can later be classified and protected
It says data quality only matters for reporting, never for core data integrity
questions.explain: A good schema diagram doesn't guarantee good data — ongoing enforcement (validation rules, duplicate tooling, deliberate required fields) matters too, and where/how sensitive data is structured has direct downstream consequences for classification and governance.
